description: This grouped bar chart illustrates the comparison of per-output and per-layer perplexity across different sparsity rates. The horizontal axis displays the categories, labeled "Sparsity Rate," and is ordered in ascending percentage increments from 10% to 80%. The vertical axis measures the values, labeled "Perplexity," and utilizes a logarithmic scale (base 10) with major tick marks and dashed horizontal gridlines at 10^1, 10^2, and 10^3, covering a visible range from just below 10^1 up to 10^3. At each sparsity rate along the horizontal axis, the chart features a grouped set of two adjacent vertical bars. According to the legend in the upper left corner, the left blue bar in each group represents "Per-Output" perplexity, while the right orange bar represents "Per-Layer" perplexity. The heights of the bars consistently increase as the sparsity rate increases from left to right. The shortest bars are found at the 10% sparsity rate, where both the blue and orange bars correspond to a value of approximately 5 to 6. The values remain relatively steady and below 10^1 until the 60% category, after which the bar heights increase significantly. The tallest bars are located at the 80% sparsity rate, where the blue "Per-Output" bar reaches an approximate value of 500 and the orange "Per-Layer" bar approaches nearly 900. The bars are sorted strictly sequentially by their ascending numerical percentage categories, and there are no bars visually emphasized with distinct shading, bolding, outlines, or specific data annotations.
